description.en: Starts work on a project: a value map before any question (who it is for, what they get, how we know), a preview of the stack, the tests and the memory it already has, the infra profile, the owner's working style and risk, then a recap with next steps and the roadmap skeleton.
description.ru: Начинает работу над проектом: карта ценности до любых вопросов (для кого, что получают, как узнаем), обзор стека, тестов и уже накопленной памяти, профиль инфраструктуры, стиль работы владельца и риск, затем итог со следующими шагами и каркасом дорожной карты.

ru: Разберись в проекте с нуля и предложи план
Подготовь старт: стек, тесты, память, инфраструктура
en: Start work on a new project
Get to know the project from scratch and propose a plan
Prepare the start: stack, tests, memory, infra

title.en: What the tree counts (only with project.start_research on)
title.ru: Что считает дерево (только при project.start_research = on)

params.counts_note: Open VALUE-MAP.md with these five lines counted from the tree itself, verbatim:
params.profile_note: Exception for this run: do not run the writer yourself. Return the infra profile as the JSON object `profile` (key: value) with only these keys: stack, test_command, release, hosts, start, deploy, logs, style; the next step stores it as the project's profile settings with the one profile writer, which refuses secrets and any other key (the same settings `bb lane-pilot profile` reads and sets).
params.recap_note: Also write .agents/planning/PROJECT.md from VALUE-MAP.md: Vision, Value and Limits (the no-gos and the risks the anamnesis names). Read .agents/planning/research/STACK.md, FEATURES.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and PITFALLS.md and the requirements before the roadmap, and build the roadmap skeleton from the requirements. A file that already exists is never overwritten: merge the new text into it keeping what is there, or leave it and write the new text to <name>.new.md next to it (it already exists and was changed by hand, or was not written by the machine: the new text is in <name>.new.md next to it).

nodes.prompt: Value map builder, before asking anything: from README, the passport (project-onboard), the site and the code — who the product is for, the job they hire it for, what they get, how we would know it works. Write .agents/planning/VALUE-MAP.md. {{tree.counts_note}}

Stack and tests: languages, frameworks, the test command and whether it is green. Memory preview: lane_pilot_memory context (what the hub corpus already knows), the memory graph of notes by area. Infra profile: hosts, start, deploy, logs, kept as the project's profile settings (`bb lane-pilot profile` is the one writer). {{tree.profile_note}}
Ask only for the fields still missing, at most five questions: audience, constraints, stack, money, deadline. No answer is a timeout — the run proceeds with the stated assumptions.

Research competitors and conventions for what the project is, from the value map and the owner's answers. Write .agents/planning/research/STACK.md, FEATURES.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and PITFALLS.md — each with its sources and what the roadmap should take from it. A file that already exists is never overwritten: merge the new text into it keeping what is there, or leave it and write the new text to <name>.new.md next to it (it already exists and was changed by hand, or was not written by the machine: the new text is in <name>.new.md next to it).

From the goal, the value map, the answers and the research: 3-7 requirements with ids into .agents/planning/REQUIREMENTS.md, the way new-milestone writes them. A file that already exists is never overwritten: merge the new text into it keeping what is there, or leave it and write the new text to <name>.new.md next to it (it already exists and was changed by hand, or was not written by the machine: the new text is in <name>.new.md next to it).

Working style and risk from the owner's anamnesis. Recap in five lines, three next steps, and the roadmap skeleton (lane-plan template fill ROADMAP, STATE; phases with lane-plan phase add). {{tree.recap_note}}
